about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Pineapple Buns
recipes.summary: Soft milky buns with a sweet, crackled cookie crust, the Hong Kong bakery classic (no pineapple inside).
steps: Mix the bread flour, caster sugar, yeast and salt, then add the warm milk, egg and 40g butter. Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and let it double.
For the topping, beat the 60g butter and icing sugar until pale, mix in the yolk, then fold in the plain flour to a soft dough. Roll into a log, wrap and chill.
Divide the risen dough into 8 balls, shape them smooth and set on a lined tray 5cm apart. Cover and prove until puffy and nearly doubled.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Slice the topping dough into 8 discs, flatten each to 8cm and drape over a bun. Score a light crisscross with a knife and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until the tops are deep golden and the buns sound hollow when tapped underneath. Cool on a rack for 10 minutes.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bun. Plus about 2 hours proving and chilling.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake the buns until fully cooked through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: best the day they are baked; keep covered for 2 days or freeze for 1 month and warm for 8 minutes at 150°C fan.

recipes.title: Melon Pan
recipes.summary: Fluffy sweet buns wrapped in a thin crisp cookie shell scored to look like a melon.
steps: Mix the bread flour, 45g sugar, yeast and salt, then add the warm milk, egg and 40g butter. Knead for 10 minutes until smooth, cover and let it double.
For the crust, beat the 60g butter and 60g sugar until pale, mix in the yolk and vanilla, then fold in the plain flour and baking powder. Chill, then divide into 8 balls.
Divide the risen dough into 8 balls. Flatten each crust ball to an 8cm disc between baking paper, press a bun into it and wrap so the dough is covered on the top and sides.
Dip the tops in the coating sugar, score a diamond pattern with a knife and set on a lined tray 5cm apart. Cover and prove until puffy.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Bake for 16 to 18 minutes until the crust is pale gold and cracked in places and the buns sound hollow underneath. Cool on a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bun. Plus about 1 hour 45 minutes proving and chilling.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake the buns until fully cooked through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: best the day they are baked; keep covered for 2 days or freeze for 1 month.

recipes.title: Hotteok
recipes.summary: Chewy yeasted pancakes stuffed with a melting cinnamon, brown sugar and walnut filling.
steps: Stir the flour, caster sugar, yeast and salt together, add the warm milk and 1 tbsp oil and mix to a sticky dough. Cover and let it double.
Stir the brown sugar, cinnamon, walnuts and sesame seeds together in a bowl until evenly combined.
Using damp hands, divide the dough into 8 balls. Flatten each ball in your palm, put 2 tbsp of the filling in the middle and pinch the edges closed.

Heat a little oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Place a ball seam side down and press flat to 10cm with an oiled spatula. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden and the sugar inside has melted.
Cool for 3 minutes before eating, as the filling is very hot.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 hotteok. Plus about 1 hour proving.
Contains tree nuts (walnuts) and sesame.
Storage: best eaten warm; keep covered for 1 day and reheat in a dry pan for 2 minutes per side.

recipes.title: Dorayaki
recipes.summary: Fluffy honey pancakes sandwiched around sweet red bean paste.
steps: Whisk the eggs, sugar and honey for 3 minutes until pale and thick. Sift in the flour and bicarbonate of soda, add the water and fold to a smooth batter.
Heat a non-stick frying pan over low heat and wipe with a little oil. Pour 2 tbsp of batter into a 7cm round and cook for 2 minutes until bubbles appear and the surface looks dry.
Flip and cook for 30 seconds until pale gold. Stack the pancakes under a clean tea towel to keep them soft and make 16 in total.
For the filling, mash the beans with the 70g sugar and simmer for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick and jammy. Cool.
Spread 1 tbsp of the bean paste on a pancake, top with a second and press gently.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 sandwich (2 pancakes). Plus 10 minutes resting the batter.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and cook each pancake until the centre is set and no longer wet; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keeps 2 days in an airtight container; the pancakes freeze well for 1 month.

recipes.title: Kuih Bahulu
recipes.summary: Tiny sponge cakes with a crisp edge and soft eggy middle, baked in a mini muffin tin.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Brush two 12-hole mini muffin tins well with oil and heat them in the oven for 5 minutes.
Whisk the eggs and sugar with an electric whisk for 8 minutes until pale, thick and tripled, with a ribbon trail.
Sift in the flour and baking powder, add the vanilla and melted butter and fold gently until just combined.
Spoon the batter into the hot tin holes until three-quarters full. Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until risen, golden and springy to the touch. Turn out onto a rack and repeat with any remaining batter.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cakes (makes 24).
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake the cakes until fully set in the middle; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: best the day they are baked; keep airtight for 3 days.

recipes.title: Kuih Keria
recipes.summary: Sweet potato doughnuts fried until crisp and rolled in a sandy sugar coating.

items: 500g orange sweet potato, peeled and cubed

steps: Boil the sweet potato for 15 minutes until very tender, drain well and mash until smooth. Mix with the flour and salt into a soft dough and shape into 24 rings, about 5cm wide, with a hole in the middle.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 170°C. Fry the rings in batches of 5 for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until golden brown and crisp. Drain on paper towel.
Boil the sugar and water for 3 minutes until it turns thick and begins to crystallise on the spoon. Take it off the heat, toss in the doughnuts and stir until coated in a dry sandy sugar.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 3 doughnuts. Plus 10 minutes cooling before shaping.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep, heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire. Let the oil cool fully before moving it.
Storage: best the day they are made; keep airtight for 1 day.

recipes.title: Onde-Onde Sweet Potato Balls
recipes.summary: Chewy sweet potato balls with a palm sugar centre, rolled in salted coconut.

items: 250g orange sweet potato, peeled and cubed

steps: Boil the sweet potato for 15 minutes until very tender, drain and mash smooth. Work in the rice flour, salt and water to a soft dough that does not stick to your hands.
Roll into 24 balls the size of a walnut. Press a hollow into each, put in a pinch of palm sugar and seal.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil. Cook the balls in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until they float, then 1 minute more. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Toss the warm balls in the coconut mixed with the 1/4 tsp salt and serve right away.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 3 balls. Plus 10 minutes cooling.
Storage: best eaten warm on the day; the palm sugar centre will be hot when freshly cooked.

recipes.title: Bibingka Muffin Cups
recipes.summary: Soft rice flour cakes with coconut milk, baked golden and finished with butter, sugar and coconut.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin.
Whisk the rice flour, baking powder and 100g sugar. Beat the eggs with the coconut milk and 60g melted butter, then mix into the dry ingredients to a smooth batter and stir in the mozzarella.
Fill the holes two-thirds full and bake for 20 minutes until the tops are set and the edges are golden.
Brush with the extra melted butter, sprinkle with the 1 tbsp sugar and coconut and grill for 2 minutes until the coconut turns golden. Cool for 5 minutes before turning out.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cakes (makes 12).
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until set in the middle with a clean skewer; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: best warm on the day; keep covered for 1 day.

recipes.title: Castella Cubes
recipes.summary: A honey-sweet Japanese sponge cake with a fine soft crumb, cut into neat cubes.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Grease a 15cm square tin and line it with baking paper.
Beat the eggs and sugar with an electric whisk for 10 minutes until pale, thick and the ribbon holds for 5 seconds. Warm the honey and milk together and fold in.
Sift in the flour in three batches and fold gently until just combined. Pour into the tin and tap it on the bench to remove large bubbles.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the top is deep golden and a skewer comes out clean. Turn out, peel off the paper and cool wrapped in baking paper. Cut into 16 cubes.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cubes.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until the centre is fully set; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep wrapped for 3 days; the flavour is best the day after baking.

recipes.title: Yakgwa
recipes.summary: Crisp-edged honey ginger cookies fried and soaked in a fragrant syrup.
steps: Rub the flour, sesame oil and salt together until sandy, add the hot water and bring to a firm dough without kneading. Roll to 1cm thick and cut into 20 diamonds.
Poke a few holes in each with a fork. Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 150°C and fry the cookies in batches for 6 to 8 minutes until deep golden, turning now and then. Drain on paper towel.
Simmer the honey, water, ginger and cinnamon for 5 minutes until slightly thickened. Soak the warm cookies in the syrup for 10 minutes, then lift onto a rack to drain.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies. Plus 10 minutes soaking.
Contains sesame.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep, heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Spiced Puff-Puff Dough Balls
recipes.summary: Soft, pillowy fried dough balls, lightly sweet and spiced with nutmeg.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and nutmeg, then stir in the warm water to a thick, stretchy batter. Cover and let it rise until doubled and bubbly.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 175°C. Drop in walnut-sized scoops of batter with a wet spoon in batches of 6 to 8.
Fry for 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until deep golden and puffed. Drain on paper towel and serve warm.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 4 balls (makes about 32). Plus about 1 hour rising.

Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire. Let the oil cool completely before moving it.
Storage: best eaten the same day.

recipes.title: Syrup-Soaked Plaited Doughnuts
recipes.summary: Plaited fried dough dunked in ice-cold syrup to give a crackling shell and sticky centre.
steps: Make the syrup first: boil the 300g sugar, water, ginger and lemon juice for 8 minutes, then chill until ice cold.

Rub the butter into the flour, baking powder and 1 tbsp sugar. Mix the egg and milk, stir in and knead to a soft dough. Rest, then roll to 1cm thick and cut into 8 strips of 3 plaits each, pinching the ends together.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 175°C. Fry the plaits in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden brown.
Lift each hot koeksister straight into the cold syrup for 1 minute, turn, then drain on a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 koeksister. Plus 2 hours chilling the syrup and 30 minutes resting.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and fry until the dough is cooked through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container in the fridge.

recipes.title: Mandazi
recipes.summary: Lightly sweet, cardamom-scented coconut doughnut triangles, a staple of East African tea breaks.
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and cardamom. Beat the egg with the coconut milk, stir in and knead briefly into a soft dough. Cover and rest.
Roll to 1cm thick, cut into 8 squares and cut each in half diagonally to make 16 triangles, then halve again if you like smaller pieces.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 175°C. Fry in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side until puffed and golden brown. Drain on paper towel.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 pieces (makes 24). Plus 20 minutes resting.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and fry until the dough is cooked through and golden; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire.
Storage: best the day they are made; keep airtight for 2 days.

recipes.title: Vetkoek with Apricot Jam
recipes.summary: Golden fried bread balls, crisp outside and soft inside, filled with apricot jam.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the warm water and knead for 5 minutes into a soft sticky dough. Cover and let it double.
Divide into 8 balls and flatten slightly.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 170°C. Fry 3 at a time for 8 to 10 minutes, turning often, until deep golden and cooked through when you tear one open.
Drain, split each open and fill with 1 tsp jam.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 1 vetkoek. Plus about 1 hour rising.

Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire. Let the oil cool completely before moving it.
Storage: best fresh; keep covered for 1 day.

recipes.title: Melktert Cups
recipes.summary: Mini sweet pastry cups filled with a cinnamon milk custard, a South African favourite.
steps: Rub the 75g butter into the flour and icing sugar, add the yolk and water and bring to a dough. Wrap and chill, then roll and cut 12 rounds to fit a 12-hole muffin tin, pressing them in.

Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Simmer 300ml milk with the cinnamon stick for 5 minutes, then remove the stick. Whisk the cornflour, sugar, egg and remaining milk in a bowl, pour in the hot milk, return to the pan and stir for 3 minutes until thick. Stir in the 15g butter and vanilla.
Spoon the custard into the pastry cases and bake for 18 to 20 minutes until the pastry is golden and the custard just set.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, dust with cinnamon and lift out.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 cup. Plus about 30 minutes chilling the pastry.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs; cook the custard until thick and bake until just set. Keep refrigerated; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days and eat within that time.

recipes.title: Hertzoggies
recipes.summary: Jam-filled pastry cups with a golden coconut meringue topping.
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and icing sugar, add the yolk and water and bring to a dough. Chill, then roll and cut 12 rounds to fit a 12-hole muffin tin, pressing them in.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Spoon 1 tsp jam into each case.
Whisk the whites to soft peaks, add the sugar a spoonful at a time and beat for 4 minutes until stiff and glossy. Fold in the coconut and spoon over the jam.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the topping is golden and the pastry is cooked underneath. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 cup. Plus about 30 minutes chilling the pastry.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake the meringue until firm and dry; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep airtight for 4 days.

recipes.title: Soetkoekies
recipes.summary: Old-fashioned spiced sweet biscuits with ginger, cinnamon and nutmeg.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays.
Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until pale, then beat in the egg. Stir in the flour, spices, baking powder and milk to a soft dough.
Roll into 20 balls, set 4cm apart on the trays and flatten with a fork.
Bake for 13 to 15 minutes until golden at the edges but still soft in the middle. Cool on the trays for 5 minutes, then on a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 biscuits.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until set; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

recipes.title: Mahamri
recipes.summary: Soft cardamom and coconut fried bread triangles from the Swahili coast.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, cardamom and salt, add the coconut milk and warm water and knead for 5 minutes into a soft dough. Cover and let it double.
Roll to 1cm thick, cut into 6 squares, halve each diagonally and cut again to make 12 triangles.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 175°C. Fry in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side until puffed and golden. Drain on paper towel.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 2 triangles. Plus about 1 hour rising.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire.
Storage: best the day they are made.

recipes.title: Luqaimat
recipes.summary: Crisp golden fried dumplings drizzled with honey, a Gulf Ramadan favourite.
steps: Mix the flour, cornflour, yeast, sugar and cardamom, add the warm water and beat for 2 minutes to a thick sticky batter. Cover and let it rise until bubbly.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 175°C. Drop in small spoonfuls of batter, using a wet spoon, in batches of 8.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until crisp and deep golden. Drain on paper towel and drizzle with honey.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 5 dumplings (makes about 40). Plus about 1 hour rising.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire.
Storage: best eaten within an hour of frying.

recipes.title: Qatayef with Ricotta and Pistachio
recipes.summary: Folded yeast pancakes filled with sweet ricotta, baked and brushed with lemon syrup.
steps: Whisk the flour, semolina, sugar, yeast, baking powder and warm water into a smooth thin batter. Cover and let it rest.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Pour in 2 tbsp batter for each 10cm pancake and cook one side only for 1 to 2 minutes until bubbles appear and the top is dry. Make 12 and cool on a tea towel.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Mix the ricotta and honey, spoon onto the cooked side of each pancake, fold over and pinch the edge closed.
Brush with melted butter and bake on a lined tray for 8 to 10 minutes until golden.
Boil the syrup sugar, water and lemon juice for 5 minutes and brush a little over the hot qatayef. Top with pistachios.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 qatayef. Plus 30 minutes resting the batter.
Contains tree nuts (pistachios).
Storage: best warm on the day; keep refrigerated for 1 day.

recipes.title: Barazek Sesame Pistachio Cookies
recipes.summary: Thin, crisp Syrian sesame cookies glazed in honey and covered with toasted seeds and pistachios.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays.
Beat the butter and sugar until pale, beat in the egg, then stir in the flour, baking powder and milk to a soft dough. Roll into 16 balls.
Warm the honey, dip the top of each ball, then press into the mixed sesame seeds and pistachios. Flatten to 6cm discs, seed side up, on the trays.
Bake for 13 to 15 minutes until golden at the edges. Cool on the trays.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies. Contains sesame and tree nuts (pistachios).
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until set; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

recipes.title: Kuli-Kuli Spiced Peanut Sticks
recipes.summary: Crunchy baked peanut sticks with ginger, paprika and chilli, inspired by Nigerian kuli-kuli.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line a tray.
Blitz the peanuts in a food processor for 1 to 2 minutes into a coarse, oily paste. Mix in the ginger, paprika, chilli, salt and water until it holds together.
Roll into 24 thin sticks, 7cm long, and set on the tray.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes, turning once, until dry and deep golden. Cool completely so they crisp up.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 3 sticks. Contains peanuts.
Storage: keep airtight for 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Nigerian Buns
recipes.summary: Dense, nutmeg-scented fried dough balls, crisp outside and soft inside.
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and nutmeg, rub in the butter, then add the beaten egg and milk and knead briefly into a soft dough. Rest, then roll into 16 balls.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 170°C. Fry in batches of 5 for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until deep golden and a ball tears open cooked through.
Drain on paper towel and cool for 5 minutes before eating.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 buns. Plus 15 minutes resting.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and fry until cooked through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire.
Storage: best the day they are made.
